articles.title: Supreme Court extends bail of two accused in 2020 Delhi riots case by three months
articles.description: Tasleem Ahmed and Abdul Khalid Saifi face charges under UAPA in the 2020 Delhi riots case. Their interim bail has been extended until February 2027.

articles.title: Syrian governors mark second anniversary of uprising that toppled Assad regime
articles.description: On the second anniversary of the Deterrence of Aggression Battle, Syrian governors commemorated the military campaign that led to the ousting of Bashar Assad's regime. They emphasized the importance of safeguarding liberation gains, initiating reforms, and facilitating the return of displaced Syrians while honoring the sacrifices made during the uprising against decades of Assad family rule.

articles.title: Court acquits 6 accused of murder during 2020 NE Delhi riots
articles.description: A Delhi court on Friday acquitted six men in a murder case during the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots, holding that the prosecution failed to prove the men’s presence during the attack or link the identification to the deceased

articles.title: France falls into recession after far-left riots break out across country in blow to Emmanuel Macron
articles.description: France has fallen into recession after the European nation's economy shrank by more than the predicted figures. Emmanuel Macron is said to be facing a crisis after the economy plunged by 0.2 per cent in the third quarter between July and September. The shrinking of France's economy is bigger than the predicted 0.1 per cent figure. New revised estimates also show figures fell in the second quarter as well as the third by 0.02 per cent. France was originally predicted to see a flatline for the same period. Following the revision of the stats, Europe’s third-largest economy now meets the definition of a technical recession. Marie Leclair of France’s statistics agency INSEE confirmed: "We now have a very slight decline in GDP in the second quarter." Senior economist at Dutch bank ING Charlotte de Montpellier said of the figures: "It has technically been in recession since the beginning of the year." She added: "The outlook for 2027 remains very gloomy. Salaried employment fell by 94,400 jobs over the past year. "The situation is even worse in the private sector, where 109,000 jobs were lost over the same period. "The weakening labour market will increasingly weigh on household confidence, income and consumption. "Financing conditions also remain difficult, while uncertainty over future taxes and public spending is exceptionally high." LATEST DEVELOPMENTS British pub manager died after 'homeless man' stabbed her in the chest at train station TV station that backed Iran regime loses UK broadcast licence after GB News investigation Autistic Briton with mental age of eight jailed abroad after being 'exploited as drug mule' France's 10-year borrowing costs last month surpassed five per cent, a new 24-year high for the economy. The country's deficit is also poised to hit 5.5 per cent of GDP this year, the highest in the euro area. The shrinking economic growth comes as Mr Macron faces growing mass protests over high fuel prices. One protester was killed, and more than 100 others were injured during the nationwide demonstrations that commenced in September. Police deployed tear gas in an attempt to disperse the protesters, the "yellow vests". Demonstrations took place in Porte Maillot, Bastille Square and Champs-Elysees in Paris. According to the interior ministry, around 244,000 people took part in around 2,000 protests across the country. A crowd of at least 1,000 protesters also gathered in front of Elysee Palace, calling for Mr Macron to resign. Ms Montpellier predicted the French will be "heading to the polls" against the backdrop of a "weakening economy" for Mr Macron. She concluded: "It is difficult to identify a driver capable of generating a meaningful recovery in domestic demand over the next few quarters. "France will enter next year without economic momentum. Even if quarterly growth turns slightly positive again, this will not be enough to produce solid annual growth. "We expect GDP to grow by just 0.4 per cent on average in 2027, with risks still tilted to the downside." Our Standards: The GB News Editorial Charter

articles.title: Postponed game, lightning strike, and riots—Beşiktaş match becomes a political issue
articles.description: A home game abroad, a flight with a layover, and clashes between fans and police: events are unfolding rapidly surrounding the Europa League match between Besiktas Istanbul and Hapoel Beer-Sheva. The game has now also become a political issue.

articles.title: Besiktas v Hapoel with lengthy interruption due to riots in the stands
articles.description: The Europa League match between Turkey's Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Be'er-Sheva on Thursday was interrupted for a lengthy period due to serious disturbances in the stands. The game had been moved to Batumi, Georgia, due to security concerns related to the Gaza War.
